notes: Annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners for the year ending June 30, 1895. Curated: the Memorial Museum's handover, Stow Lake's origin, the prayer-book cross.

coverage.remaining: Not placed or already on the pages: Recreation Valley rebuilt after the Midwinter Fair, the pumping station's settling reservoir, the first mile of bicycle road from Broom Point and of the Great Highway boulevard, Huntington Falls ($25,000, C. P. Huntington; no page), Sweeney's Observatory, the Conservatory (fire year given as 1882, against 1883 on the page), the proposed Goethe-Schiller monument and Grant bust.

findings.description: Before nearly three thousand people on Saturday, March 23, 1895, M. H. de Young, Director-General of the Midwinter Fair, handed the Park Commissioners the fair's Art Building and its annex with their contents, a golden key with them, as the Memorial Museum; part of the annex reproduced the Royal Bavarian pavilion, with vaulted ceiling and frescoed panels.

findings.description: Recording the death of their president W. W. Stow, the Park Commissioners told how the lake that bears his name began as a reservoir on the east side of Strawberry Hill, badly needed in case the pumps failed, and was made an ornamental lake at his instance as well, with a pipe from the Almshouse artesian well feeding it without pumping.

findings.description: The prayer-book cross on its hilltop was the gift of the late George W. Childs of Philadelphia, put up to mark the first reading of the Episcopal service on the Pacific coast, by the chaplain of Sir Francis Drake.
